status: eight halls in the route; six chapters preserved
summary: What actually changes when a machine appears to learn? Keep the eight-hall progression and strengthen two comparisons: repeat a loss experiment, then ask the same four centres to divide different populations. Memory and Generative return to the museum as clearly identified diagrams. Only Gradient Landscape and Classification receive manuscript edits.

items.title: Let the reader try the alternative
items.description: The Classification chapter proposed rings as a future experiment. DATASET now cycles BLOBS, RINGS and BLOCK while keeping four centres. STEP, PAUSE / RUN and RESET make the updates and repeated beginnings available. An entrance bay gives this primary encounter space; the older rooms and supporting works continue behind it.
captions: BLOBS · three planted groups meet a demand for four centres.
RINGS · the colour boundaries cut across the form we follow with our eyes.
BLOCK · a sample without planted clusters is still divided into four groups.
items.image_note: Three states of the revised artifact in the actual Godot museum, using the same raised overview camera. Each dataset is reset and given eight step attempts; convergence can halt it sooner. These are not before/after software versions, and tracked-hand interaction has not been tested.
items.before: Imagine replacing the separated blobs with two nested rings. Nearest-centre regions would divide space according to a different geometry from the rings’ apparent membership. That is a proposed alternative dataset for the room: a way to make the representation’s limits visible, rather than simply declaring that clustering is biased.
items.after:
Press DATASET to replace the blobs with RINGS. Four centres remain. Before stepping, follow a ring with your eye; then watch where its colour breaks. The grouping follows distance to a centre, which need not follow the form you were tracing.

Press DATASET again for BLOCK, a sample with no planted clusters. The procedure still gives it four groups. Does the confidence of the colour change when there was no group for it to discover? Return to BLOBS and the earlier sample returns. We have changed what the procedure encounters while keeping its demand for four centres. The boundary belongs to that meeting.

items.title: Something must hold still
items.description: The loss comparator previously redrew observations on RESET. It now repeats the selected data, starts and timer. Raising OUTLIERS introduces nested substitutions from a fixed set; unchanged observations stay put. The comparison has been raised and enlarged so the reset control is above the floor.
captions: Current loss comparison · three scoring surfaces on a raised plinth.
items.image_note: Actual museum capture and a tested approach, not a before/after pair. The surrounding legacy displays still make this a busy room; clearer separation is recorded for a later staging pass.
items.before: The squared-error surface punishes a large residual much more heavily than a small one. Huber loss is quadratic near zero and becomes linear for sufficiently large residuals. An unusual observation can therefore pull the two fitted lines differently. The outlier control helps make that difference visible while the basic task remains the same.
items.after: The squared-error surface punishes a large residual much more heavily than a small one. Huber loss is quadratic near zero and becomes linear for sufficiently large residuals. An unusual observation can therefore pull the two fitted lines differently. Raising OUTLIERS replaces more observations with fixed outlying values; it keeps the other observations and the outliers already introduced. Return the slider to an earlier setting and its sample returns too. We need something to hold still if we want to notice what a different judgement does.

items.title: Restore the diagrams and name their limits
items.description: Memory and Generative were present in the manuscript but missing from the authored museum route. Both return. Their chapters already distinguish a diagram from trained behaviour, so they stay unchanged. Generative now shows its missing reference/candidate particles and updates its explicitly scripted score display.
